channel.title: Tempo — Blog
channel.description: Notes from building Tempo, the macOS event hub for your homelab.

item.title: Announcing UniFi Protect in Tempo
item.description: UniFi Protect joins UniFi Network as a built-in source — Tempo renders the motion thumbnail inline in the action panel, with a bounded image cache so the database stays sane.

item.title: Is Tempo vibecoded?
item.description: Tempo is AI-assisted, but not vibecoded. Here's the difference, with concrete examples from how I built it.

item.title: Endless possibilities, by design
item.description: Tempo doesn't know about your specific tools. It reads the JSON payload you send and adapts the UI to whatever fields are there. The sender writes the buttons.

item.title: Why we call them scores
item.description: A note on the musical name behind Tempo's building blocks — and the shortlist of scores shipping at launch.

item.title: Great News — Tempo v1 goes freeware!
item.description: Tempo v1 will ship as freeware, forever. Here's how the community will shape what comes next — and an honest look at the costs behind it.

item.title: Dev Log #1 — Engineering notes
item.description: A first look at the engineering choices behind Tempo: ingestion schema, security model, event dimensions, and what ships at v1.

item.title: What Tempo is not
item.description: Before launch, a clear look at what Tempo deliberately isn't — and why that matters.

item.title: Who am I?
item.description: An introduction to who I am, why I built Tempo, and the philosophy behind it.
